summary: The ability to interpret the mental state of another agent based on its behavior, also called Theory of Mind (ToM), is crucial for humans in any kind of social interaction. summary: Neural language models (LMs) perform well on tasks that require sensitivity to syntactic structure. Drawing on the syntactic priming paradigm from psycholinguistics, we propose a novel technique to analyze the representations that enable such success. summary: State of the art algorithms for many pattern recognition problems rely on deep network models. summary: Large neural language models trained on massive amounts of text have emerged as a formidable strategy for Natural Language Understanding tasks. summary: Most previous studies on multi-agent reinforcement learning focus on deriving decentralized and cooperative policies to maximize a common reward and rarely consider the transferability of trained policies to new tasks. summary: In a multi-agent setting, the optimal policy of a single agent is largely dependent on the behavior of other agents. summary: Although deep reinforcement learning agents have produced impressive results in many domains, their decision making is difficult to explain to humans.
